summary: Corrected the stale daily_revenue catalog description using the matching dbt schema and model definition.

findings.claim: The catalog override describes revenue from all orders, while the model filters to completed orders and the dbt schema says refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.

evidence.fact: The original daily_revenue description said revenue comes from all orders.
The model filters with status = 'completed' and groups results by order_date.
The dbt schema documents completed-order revenue at one row per order date, excluding refunded and cancelled orders.
The manifest identifies daily_revenue as a model depending on stg_orders and records its schema description and order_date grain.

action.value: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.
action.rationale: Align the overriding catalog description with the model filter and dbt schema description.

verification.equals: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.

changes_made.description: Updated daily_revenue.description to match the model and dbt schema.

verification_performed.command: python -c "import json; c=json.load(open('project/catalog/catalog.json')); o=json.load(open('project/catalog/overrides.json')); a=next(x for x in c['assets'] if x['name']=='daily_revenue'); a.update(o.get('assets',{}).get('daily_revenue',{})); expected='Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.'; assert a['description']==expected; print('effective daily_revenue.description verified:', a['description'])"
verification_performed.result: Passed; the effective description matches the expected value.
